title: Agent Space Protocol
description: Every message of the Agent Space Protocol. Generated from schema.ts; do not edit by hand.

Accepted.description: An action has been accepted and is under way.

id.description:
The ID of a request: an action, an edit or any other message that expects an answer.
Unique for the participant that sends it, for at least as long as the space keeps its record.

seq.description: The sequence number of the action's own record entry.

Act.description:
An action. Answered by intermediate states and exactly one final `outcome`. Sending the same ID
again only returns the first outcome or the current intermediate state.

verb.description: The verb, named in the vocabulary.

args.description: The parameters, as the verb's schema describes.

basis.description: The record sequence number of the observation the action is based on.

deadline.description:
How long the action may take, in seconds from when the space receives it. When it passes

BlobRequest.description: Fetch large content by hash. Answered with `blob`.

Cancel.description:
Ask to cancel an action or edit of this participant. Cancelling is only a request: the action
still gets its own final outcome, `cancelled` if it stopped, `done` if it finished first, or
`unknown`. Has no ID and no answer of its own.

action.description: The ID of the action, edit or stream to cancel.

Capabilities.description:
The capability table of a space, declared item by item. A capability that is not declared is
unsupported: using it gets `refused` with the reason `unsupported` (or, for a message without
an ID, an `error` with the code `unsupported`). A capability declared with an empty object is
read at its most conservative value.

state.description: Where the state is: `held` by the space itself, or `external`, reached by an adapter.

lifetime.description: Whether the space lasts or is thrown away after use.

forms.description:
The observation forms the space offers. `structure` is always available and need not be
listed. Each name refers to a form declared in the vocabulary, which gives its media type.

inputs.description: The media types an action's parameters may carry, such as `audio/ogg` or `image/png`.

episode.description: Episodes started from a task and a seed.

consent.description: Actions that wait for another participant's agreement before they run.

pause.description: Holding an action under way and continuing it later.

views.description: The space's own interfaces, for hosts to embed.

Change.description: One structured change of an edit. Namespaced kinds of change may be declared by a space.

verbs.description: The verbs that wait for consent, by verb name.

ConsentMessage.description: Capability `consent`: agree to or refuse a waiting action. Answered with an `outcome`.

act.description: The sequence number of the waiting action's record entry.

by.description: The role whose presences may agree.

seconds.description:
How long the space waits, in seconds. A consent nobody answers in this time ends the action

line.description: One line saying what must hold.

DefaultOutcome.description: The default outcome of a verb.

Door.description: A door: a thing on this side that points to another space.

space.description: The identity of the space on the other side, which signs its passes.

takes.description: Whether the space accepts things handed over from other spaces.

Edit.description: An edit: structured changes, or a sentence. Gets a final outcome like an action.

id.description:
The ID of a request: an action, an edit or any other message that expects an answer.
Unique for the participant that sends it, for at least as long as the space keeps its record.

sentence.description: A sentence, translated by the space into structured changes.

basis.description: The observation the edit is based on.

deadline.description: How long the edit may take, in seconds.

roles.description: The roles that may edit. Each must also have `edit: true` in its role.

changes.description: The kinds of change accepted: `add`, `set`, `remove`, `relate`, `unrelate`, or namespaced kinds.

sentences.description: Whether edits written as a sentence are taken.

Effect.description: An effect that did happen, listed by `failed`, `cancelled` and `unknown`.

thing.description: The thing affected, when there is one.

EffectClass.description:
The class of a verb's effect, from which a participant decides whether to ask its owner first.

- `read`: reads only.
- `change`: changes this space.
- `send`: sends to others: a new recipient, forwarding, publishing.
- `spend`: spends money.
- `irreversible`: cannot be undone.

End.description:
The five final outcomes.

- `done`: carried out; has the result and the events it caused.
- `refused`: nothing happened; decided before any effect.
- `failed`: tried and not achieved; lists the effects that did happen.
- `cancelled`: confirmed stopped; lists the effects from before it stopped.
- `unknown`: may or may not have happened; says what is known and what is not confirmed.

Entries.description: Entries of the record, projected for this presence.

id.description:
The ID of a request: an action, an edit or any other message that expects an answer.
Unique for the participant that sends it, for at least as long as the space keeps its record.

more.description: Whether more entries match than were returned.

Entry.description:
One entry of the record. The envelope follows CloudEvents 1.0 in its JSON format: `id`,
`source`, `type` and `specversion` are always present. ASP adds `seq`, `aspcore`, `cause`,
`things` and `roles`.

id.description: The entry's ID: its sequence number written as a decimal string.

type.description:
The kind of entry. Kinds of the protocol start with `asp.`; the space's own kinds of event
are named in its vocabulary.

aspcore.description: The version of the core part the entry was written with.

cause.description: The sequence number of the entry that led to this one, so anything can be traced back to where it started.

roles.description: If present, only these roles receive the entry.

datacontenttype.description: The media type of `data`, `application/json` when absent.

dataref.description: Large content stored only as a hash and fetched with `blob`.

EntrySource.description:
The source of a record entry: `space` for the space itself, `presence/<presence>` for a
participant's presence, and `outside` or `outside/<who>` for participants outside the protocol.

tasks.description: The tasks an episode can be started from.

evaluator.description: The role that receives scores. Defaults to `evaluator`.

EpisodeRequest.description: Capability `episode`: start an episode from a task and a seed.

ErrorMessage.description:
A protocol error, only for messages without an ID (such as `hello` or `cancel`). A message
with an ID is always answered with an outcome instead.

code.description: A protocol reason, or a namespaced code.

about.description: The type of the message the error is about.

data.description: The content of the event, as a JSON Schema.

perceived.description: Who perceives it: everyone, or only those within range of the things involved.

EventMessage.description: A record entry pushed to a subscribed presence, or the closing event pushed to every connection.

FormContent.description: One observation in a form other than structure. Either `data` or `blob` is present.

media.description: The media type, as declared for the form in the vocabulary.

data.description: The content: text as is, binary content as base64.

blob.description: Large content stored by hash and fetched with `blob`.

media.description: The media type of the form.

continuous.description: Whether it is continuous, subscribed to as a stream.

n.description: The frame's number in the stream, from 0.

Hash.description:
A content hash: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits. Structured content is
hashed in its RFC 8785 canonical JSON form.

Hidden.description: What a role does not see.

properties.description: Property names left out of every thing this role observes.

events.description: Kinds of record entries this role never receives.

Identity.description:
The identity of a participant or a space: `ed25519:` followed by the unpadded base64url form of
the 32-byte Ed25519 public key. A participant that connects with a local token is shown as
`token:<name>`; one with neither is anonymous and is known only by its presence.

Join.description:
Start a presence, or resume one after a disconnect. Answered with an `outcome` whose result is a
`JoinResult`.

role.description: The role asked for. The space decides the role given.

proof.description:
Proof of identity: the unpadded base64url Ed25519 signature, by the key named in `hello`, of

resume.description: Resume a presence kept after a disconnect, with the token from its `JoinResult`.

pass.description: A pass signed by another space, for a participant arriving through a door.

participant.description: The participant's identity as the space knows it.

presentation.description: What was done with each presentation preference.

head.description: The latest record sequence number when the presence started.

Offer.description:
Capability `doors`: hand a thing over to this space, or ask to pass through one of its doors.

- With `thing`, the sender (another space, acting as a participant) offers the thing; the outcome
  is `done` once this space has taken it and recorded `asp.take`, with an `OfferResult`.
- With `door` and no `thing`, a participant asks to pass through the door; the outcome is `done`
  with a `PassResult`, and the presence ends here.

PartName.description:
The names of the parts of the protocol. `core` covers entering, observing, acting, editing,
outcomes, events, the record and the vocabulary. Every other part belongs to the capability of
the same name. A part name outside this list must carry a namespace.

ProtocolReason.description:
The reasons defined by the protocol. Any other reason code carries a namespace.

- `unsupported`: a capability, part, message or verb the space does not have.
- `forbidden`: the presence's role may not do this.
- `malformed`: the message does not match the schema or the verb's parameters.
- `stale`: the observation named by `basis` is out of date and the verb refuses stale actions.
- `constraint`: the change would break a constraint; nothing was changed.
- `deadline`: the deadline, or the time to wait for consent, passed.
- `closed`: the space closed, or the presence ended.
- `restarted`: the space restarted and could not confirm the outcome.
- `expired`: the record no longer keeps what was asked for.

SpaceHello.description:
The space's half of the handshake. It gives the negotiated version of each part, the capability
table, the hash of the vocabulary, the state of the record and a random value the participant
